== No Name on the Work Roll (completed)
- I woke in the hold of a ship, moored at a pier west of Lilmoth in Black Marsh, among a gang of Argonians I do not know. I'm to go up the stairs and out of the door to the pier, and speak to the man who stands there.
- Buys-The-Months, the broker, holds his gang's Owing, the months of work they owe. I am on no line of his roll, so he will not keep me. He says Nesh-Deeka, a guest at Salts-The-Catch's house south of the second big ship off Lilmoth's dock, pays for work. I'm to find her there, east along the shore.
- A woman with a knotted cord killed Nesh-Deeka's courier at the gang's camp the night it burned, took his satchel and let me live. Nesh-Deeka serves the Veiled Reed, the state's quiet service, and wants a hand whose name is on no roll. I'm to hear her out and say whether I will work for the Reed.
- I took work with the Veiled Reed, and Nesh-Deeka put fifty gold in my hand. She has told me the first work the Reed wants of me. Why the woman with the knotted cord let me live, I still do not know.
== The Cutters' Jar
- Nesh-Deeka gave me the Veiled Reed's first work. Dives-Without-A-Rope, one of the broker's gang, carried off a jar of sap that the cutters dropped at the burnt camp. Nesh-Deeka wants it to learn what the cutters wanted. I'm to ask Dives-Without-A-Rope for the jar in the ship's hold at the pier west of Lilmoth.
- I paid Dives-Without-A-Rope twenty gold. She gave me the key to her lockbox in the ship's hold. I'm to take the jar from the lockbox and bring it to Nesh-Deeka.
Objectives:
  [ ] Bring the jar from Dives-Without-A-Rope's lockbox to Nesh-Deeka.

It is in the hold of the ship of Buys-The-Months, at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth. Go west along the shore, a fair way, past the old lighthouse. Dives-Without-A-Rope keeps it in the hold. How you get it is your affair. Look over the hold before you decide. Then bring the jar to me here."

Nesh-Deeka: "That is the jar. Let me draw the stopper. The sap is fresh from the roots. It was drawn into a jar that the cutters brought with them, so they mean to keep it. This is a long work, not a raid. Whoever tastes Hist sap sees a vision. A stranger may see something else. I do not know which you are. I will write while you put one drop on your tongue. Will you taste it?"

Nesh-Deeka: "Good. Be still. I will write while you are under it. A ship's hold. Roots through the deck. A door that was never built. A dry voice with no words in it. You said all of it aloud, and I wrote it on the page. I do not know what it means. I will not guess. Keep the page. Twenty-five gold is yours, and I take the jar. We pay our hands. I have heard that the Hist at Low-Reed Village, east of Lilmoth, has turned its face away."
